248	resolve_version_from_github() {
249	    local channel="$1" version
250	    if [[ "$channel" == "nightly" ]]; then
251	        # The literal -nightly. segment, not a bare "nightly" substring: a
252	        # looser match here selects tags every other reader rejects, so the two
253	        # origins in this script would disagree about what is installable.
254	        version="$(fetch_github_json "${GITHUB_API}/releases?per_page=20" \
255	            | grep '"tag_name"' \
256	            | grep -- '-nightly\.' \
257	            | head -n 1 \
258	            | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/' || true)"
259	    else
260	        version="$(fetch_github_json "${GITHUB_API}/releases/latest" \
261	            | grep '"tag_name"' \
262	            | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/' || true)"
263	    fi
264	
265	    # Validated exactly like the release origin's answer. An origin we do not
266	    # own is not more trustworthy than one we do.
267	    if [[ -n "$version" ]] && version_valid_for_channel "$version" "$channel"; then
268	        printf '%s' "$version"
269	        return 0
270	    fi
271	    return 1
272	}
273	
274	resolve_version_from_origin() {
275	    case "$1" in
276	        entire) resolve_version_from_entire "$2" ;;
277	        github) resolve_version_from_github "$2" ;;
278	        *)      return 1 ;;
279	    esac
280	}
281	
282	# resolve_version walks the origins and prints the first version any of them
283	# names. Failing to reach one origin is not fatal; failing to reach all of them
284	# is.
285	resolve_version() {
286	    local channel="$1"
287	    local origin version
288	    for origin in $(release_origins); do
289	        version="$(resolve_version_from_origin "$origin" "$channel" || true)"
290	        if [[ -n "$version" ]]; then
291	            printf '%s' "$version"
292	            return 0
293	        fi
294	    done
295	    return 1
296	}
297	
298	download_file() {
299	    local url="$1"
300	    local output="$2"
301	    local curl_opts=(-fsSL "${CURL_DOWNLOAD_OPTS[@]}")
302	
303	    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" -o "$output"
304	}
305	
306	verify_checksum() {
307	    local file="$1"
308	    local expected_checksum="$2"
309	    local actual_checksum
310	
311	    if command -v sha256sum &> /dev/null; then
312	        actual_checksum=$(sha256sum "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
313	    elif command -v shasum &> /dev/null; then
314	        actual_checksum=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
315	    else
316	        warn "No checksum tool found (sha256sum or shasum). Skipping verification."
317	        return 0
318	    fi
319	
320	    if [[ "$actual_checksum" != "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
321	        error "Checksum verification failed!  Expected: $expected_checksum, actual: $actual_checksum"
322	    fi
323	}
324	
325	# fetch_release_from_origin downloads the archive and checksums.txt for one
326	# version from a single origin and verifies one against the other.
327	#
328	# Archive and checksums always come from the SAME origin. Mixing them would let
329	# a healthy origin's checksums vouch for another origin's bytes, which is a
330	# weaker guarantee than either origin offers on its own.
331	#
332	# Return codes drive the caller's chain, and the split follows the same rule as
333	# the checkpoint read chain: a definite bad answer aborts, an unreachable one
334	# advances.
335	#   0  archive downloaded and verified
336	#   1  this origin could not serve the release — try the next one
337	# A checksum MISMATCH does not return: it calls error and exits. Bytes that
338	# disagree with their own origin's checksums mean that origin is corrupt or
339	# hostile, and quietly retrying elsewhere would hide it.
340	fetch_release_from_origin() {
341	    local origin="$1" version="$2" archive_name="$3" tmp_dir="$4"
342	    local base label archive_path checksums_path expected_checksum
343	    base="$(origin_artifact_base "$origin")"
344	    label="$(origin_label "$origin")"
345	    archive_path="${tmp_dir}/${archive_name}"
346	    checksums_path="${tmp_dir}/checksums.txt"
347	
348	    info "Downloading ${archive_name} from ${label}..."
349	    if ! download_file "${base}/v${version}/${archive_name}" "$archive_path"; then
350	        warn "Could not download ${archive_name} from ${label}"
351	        return 1
352	    fi
353	
354	    if ! download_file "${base}/v${version}/checksums.txt" "$checksums_path"; then
355	        warn "Could not download checksums.txt from ${label}"
356	        return 1
357	    fi
358	
359	    expected_checksum=$(grep -iE "${archive_name}\$" "$checksums_path" | awk '{print $1}' || true)
360	    if [[ -z "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
361	        warn "checksums.txt from ${label} does not list ${archive_name}"
362	        return 1
363	    fi
364	
365	    info "Verifying checksum..."
366	    verify_checksum "$archive_path" "$expected_checksum"
367	    success "Checksum verified (${label})"
368	    return 0
369	}

371	main() {
372	    local channel="${DEFAULT_CHANNEL}"
373	    local channel_given=0
374	    local version=""
375	
376	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
377	        case "$1" in
378	            --channel)
379	                shift
380	                [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || error "--channel requires a value"
381	                channel="$1"
382	                channel_given=1
383	                ;;
384	            --version)

386	                [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || error "--version requires a value"
387	                version="${1#v}"
388	                ;;
389	            -h|--help)
390	                usage
391	                exit 0
392	                ;;
393	            *)
394	                error "Unknown argument: $1"
395	                ;;
396	        esac
397	        shift
398	    done
399	
400	    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
401	        error "curl is required but not installed. Please install curl and try again."
402	    fi
403	
404	    case "$channel" in
405	        stable|nightly) ;;
406	        *)
407	            error "Unsupported channel: ${channel}. Expected 'stable' or 'nightly'."
408	            ;;
409	    esac
410	
411	    # --version pins a specific build and skips discovery, so it cannot also
412	    # honour --channel. Silently installing a stable build under
413	    # `--channel nightly --version X` is the worst outcome; refusing is better
414	    # than guessing which half of a contradictory request was meant.
415	    if [[ -n "$version" ]]; then
416	        if ! version_is_release_version "$version"; then
417	            error "--version ${version} is not a version. Expected X.Y.Z, optionally with a prerelease suffix."
418	        fi
419	        if [[ "$channel_given" -eq 1 ]] && ! version_valid_for_channel "$version" "$channel"; then
420	            error "--version ${version} is not a ${channel} version. Drop --channel to install it, or pick a ${channel} version."
421	        fi
422	    fi
423	
424	    info "Installing Entire CLI..."
425	
426	    # Detect platform
427	    local os arch
428	    os=$(detect_os)
429	    arch=$(detect_arch)
430	    info "Detected platform: ${os}/${arch}"
431	
432	    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
433	        info "Fetching latest ${channel} version..."
434	        version="$(resolve_version "$channel" || true)"
435	        if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
436	            error "Could not determine the latest ${channel} version from any release origin.
437	  Tried: $(for o in $(release_origins); do printf '%s ' "$(origin_label "$o")"; done)
438	  Check your internet connection, or install a known version directly:
439	    curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --version X.Y.Z"
440	        fi
441	    fi
442	    # Strip leading 'v' if present
443	    version="${version#v}"
444	    info "Installing version: ${version}"
445	
446	    local archive_name="entire_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
447	
448	    tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
449	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT
450	
451	    local origin fetched=0
452	    for origin in $(release_origins); do
453	        if fetch_release_from_origin "$origin" "$version" "$archive_name" "$tmp_dir"; then
454	            fetched=1
455	            break
456	        fi
457	    done
458	    if [[ "$fetched" -ne 1 ]]; then
459	        error "Could not download Entire CLI v${version} from any release origin.
460	  Tried: $(for o in $(release_origins); do printf '%s ' "$(origin_label "$o")"; done)
461	  Check that the version exists and try again."
462	    fi
463	
464	    local archive_path="${tmp_dir}/${archive_name}"
465	
466	    info "Extracting..."
467	    tar -xzf "$archive_path" -C "$tmp_dir"
468	
469	    local install_dir="${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}"
470	    local binary_path="${tmp_dir}/entire"
471	
472	    chmod +x "$binary_path"
473	
474	    info "Installing to ${install_dir}..."
475	    local install_path="${install_dir}/entire"
476	
477	    mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
478	    info "Directory ready"
479	
480	    if [[ ! -w "$install_dir" ]]; then
481	        error "Cannot write to ${install_dir}."
482	    fi
483	    mv "$binary_path" "$install_path"
484	
485	    # Install the git remote helper binary alongside entire so
486	    # `git clone entire://…` resolves it on PATH. It ships in the same
487	    # archive as a separate binary.
488	    if [[ -f "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" ]]; then
489	        chmod +x "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire"
490	        mv "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" "${install_dir}/git-remote-entire"
491	    else
492	        warn "git-remote-entire not found in archive; entire:// clones won't work until the next release includes it."
493	    fi
494	
495	    # Verify installation
496	    if "$install_path" version &> /dev/null; then
497	        success "Entire CLI installed to ${install_path}"
498	    else
499	        error "Installation completed but the binary failed to execute. Please check the installation."
500	    fi
501	
502	    # Check if the installed binary is the one that will be found in PATH
503	    local path_binary
504	    path_binary=$(command -v "entire" 2>/dev/null || true)
505	    if [[ -n "$path_binary" && ! "$path_binary" -ef "$install_path" ]]; then
506	        # This case is a bit weird, because some other 'entire' is found on PATH.  Warn user.
507	        echo ""
508	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} ${BOLD}WARNING: PATH conflict detected${NC}"
509	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
510	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Installed to: ${install_path}"
511	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} But 'entire' resolves to: ${path_binary}"
512	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
513	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Your PATH may have another version of Entire CLI. To fix:"
514	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   1. Remove the old binary: rm ${path_binary}"
515	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   or"
516	        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   2. Adjust your PATH to prioritize ${install_dir}"
517	        echo ""
518	        error "Installation completed but PATH needs adjustment. Then, rerun the installation."
519	    elif [[ -z "$path_binary" ]]; then
520	        # First-time install: ~/.local/bin likely isn't on their PATH yet.
521	        # Detect their shell and show the right config file.
522	        local shell_name shell_config
523	        shell_name="$(basename "${SHELL:-}")"
524	        case "$shell_name" in
525	            zsh)
526	                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
527	                shell_config="~/.zshrc" ;;
528	            bash)
529	                if [[ -f "$HOME/.bash_profile" ]]; then
530	                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
531	                    shell_config="~/.bash_profile"
532	                else
533	                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
534	                    shell_config="~/.bashrc"
535	                fi
536	                ;;
537	            fish)
538	                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
539	                shell_config="~/.config/fish/config.fish" ;;
540	            *)
541	                shell_config="" ;;
542	        esac
543	
544	        echo ""
545	        echo -e "  Add ${BOLD}entire${NC} to your PATH:"
546	        echo ""
547	        if [[ "$shell_name" == "fish" ]]; then
548	            echo -e "    ${BOLD}mkdir -p ~/.config/fish${NC}"
549	            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'fish_add_path ${install_dir}' >> \$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish${NC}"
550	        elif [[ -n "$shell_config" ]]; then
551	            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\"' >> ${shell_config}${NC}"
552	        else
553	            echo -e "  Add this to your shell config:"

556	            echo ""

558	            exit 0
559	        fi
560	        echo ""
561	        echo -e "  Restart your terminal, then run ${BOLD}entire${NC} to get started."
562	        exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One-line installer for Entire Brain.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash
#
# Downloads a released binary for this platform, verifies it against the
# release checksums, and registers it with the Entire CLI. No Go toolchain and
# no C compiler: Brain's default build is pure Go, so the published binary runs
# as-is. Use scripts/install.sh instead when you want to build from source.
set -euo pipefail

GITHUB_REPO="entireio/entire-brain"
DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="${ENTIRE_BRAIN_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
CHANNEL="stable"

if [ -t 1 ] && [ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]; then
  BOLD=$'\033[1m'; GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'; RED=$'\033[0;31m'; YELLOW=$'\033[0;33m'; NC=$'\033[0m'
else
  BOLD=""; GREEN=""; RED=""; YELLOW=""; NC=""
fi
info()  { printf '%s==>%s %s\n' "$GREEN" "$NC" "$*"; }
warn()  { printf '%s!%s   %s\n' "$YELLOW" "$NC" "$*" >&2; }
error() { printf '%serror:%s %s\n' "$RED" "$NC" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
  # Kept inline rather than read back out of $0: the documented invocation is
  # curl | bash, where $0 is "bash" and there is no script file to read.
  cat <<'USAGE'
Install Entire Brain.

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash

Options:
  --nightly          Install the newest nightly prerelease instead of stable
  --version vX.Y.Z   Install a specific release
  --dir <path>       Install somewhere other than ~/.local/bin
  -h, --help         Show this message

The download is verified against the release checksums. Brain's default build
is pure Go, so no Go toolchain and no C compiler are needed.
USAGE
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --nightly) CHANNEL="nightly"; shift ;;
    --version) WANT_VERSION="${2:?--version needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dir)     DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="${2:?--dir needs a path}"; shift 2 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) error "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
done

for c in curl tar uname; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null || error "missing required command: $c"
done

# ---- platform ----------------------------------------------------------
os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
case "$os" in
  linux|darwin) : ;;
  *) error "unsupported OS: $os. Windows users: download the .zip from
  https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest" ;;
esac
arch="$(uname -m)"
case "$arch" in
  x86_64|amd64) arch="amd64" ;;
  arm64|aarch64) arch="arm64" ;;
  *) error "unsupported architecture: $arch" ;;
esac

if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then
  have="$(cd "$tmp" && sha256sum "$asset" | awk '{print $1}')"
elif command -v shasum >/dev/null; then
  have="$(cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 "$asset" | awk '{print $1}')"
else
  error "no sha256sum or shasum on PATH, so the download cannot be verified.
  Install coreutils (Linux) or use the system shasum (macOS), then re-run."
fi

# pipefail would make a no-match grep (exit 1) kill the script at this
# assignment, so the error below would never print. Contain it here.
want="$({ grep " ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/checksums.txt" || true; } | awk '{print $1}' | head -1)"
[ -n "$want" ] || error "checksums.txt has no entry for ${asset}
  The release may have been published with different asset names.
  Assets: https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/tag/${version}"
[ "$have" = "$want" ] || error "checksum mismatch for ${asset}
  expected ${want}
  got      ${have}"
info "checksum verified"

tar -xzf "${tmp}/${asset}" -C "$tmp"
[ -f "${tmp}/entire-brain" ] || error "archive did not contain entire-brain"
chmod +x "${tmp}/entire-brain"

mkdir -p "$DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR"
mv "${tmp}/entire-brain" "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain"
info "installed to ${BOLD}${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain${NC}"

# ---- register with the Entire CLI --------------------------------------
if command -v entire >/dev/null; then
  if entire plugin install "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain" --force >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    info "registered with the Entire CLI"
    echo
    entire brain version 2>/dev/null || true
    echo
    if ! entire graph version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      warn "Entire Graph is not installed. Brain uses it for code analysis, and
  setup will report the semantic index as unavailable without it:
  entire plugin install graph"
    fi
    printf '%sNext:%s  entire brain setup     (in a Git repository)\n' "$BOLD" "$NC"
  else
    warn "could not register the plugin automatically. Run:
  entire plugin install ${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain --force"
  fi
else
  warn "the Entire CLI was not found on PATH. Install it first:
  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
then run:
  entire plugin install ${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}/entire-brain --force"
fi

case ":${PATH}:" in
  *":${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}:"*) : ;;
  *) warn "${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR} is not on your PATH. Add:
  export PATH=\"${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}:\$PATH\"" ;;
esac

"""Regression tests for the release path.

Both of these encode a defect the agent review found on the pull request that
introduced the release workflow and the standalone installer. They are written
to fail if either defect is reintroduced, not to describe the fix.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
WORKFLOWS = REPO / ".github" / "workflows"
INSTALLER = REPO / "scripts" / "get-brain.sh"

# Every form a run: script can take. Matching only "run: |" left the single
# line form, the chomping forms and folded scalars unscanned — which is most of
# the run: keys in test.yml, and exactly where a new one would be added.
RUN_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<indent> +)run:[ \t]*(?:"
    r"(?P<inline>[^|>\n][^\n]*)\n"                       # run: echo ...
    r"|[|>][+-]?[ \t]*\n(?P<body>(?:(?P=indent) .*\n|[ \t]*\n)*)"  # run: | / |- / > / >-
    r")",
    re.M,
)


def run_script_lines(source):
    """Yield (line_number, text) for every line of every run: script."""
    for block in RUN_BLOCK.finditer(source):
        start = source[: block.start()].count("\n") + 1
        if block.group("inline"):
            yield start, block.group("inline")
        else:
            for offset, line in enumerate((block.group("body") or "").splitlines()):
                yield start + offset + 1, line


# Contexts whose value someone outside the repository can influence. These are
# the ones that become code when interpolated into a shell script. Values
# GitHub computes itself — github.sha, runner.temp, a fixed matrix entry — are
# not attacker-controlled and are left alone deliberately: a check that flagged
# them too would be noise, and noise gets switched off.
UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS = re.compile(
    r"\$\{\{\s*(inputs\.|github\.event\.|github\.head_ref|github\.ref_name)"
)


class WorkflowExpressionHygiene(unittest.TestCase):
    """A ${{ }} expression inside run: is substituted as text before the shell
    parses the script, so any value an attacker controls becomes code. Untrusted
    input must reach the shell through env:, where it is an ordinary string."""

    def test_no_untrusted_expression_interpolated_into_a_run_block(self) -> None:
        offenders: list[str] = []
        for workflow in sorted(WORKFLOWS.glob("*.yml")):
            source = workflow.read_text()
            for line_no, line in run_script_lines(source):
                if UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS.search(line):
                    offenders.append(f"{workflow.name}:{line_no}: {line.strip()}")

        self.assertEqual(
            offenders,
            [],
            "Attacker-influenced GitHub Actions expressions must be passed through "
            "env: rather than interpolated into a run: script:\n  " + "\n  ".join(offenders),
        )

    def test_every_job_that_consumes_the_version_validates_its_shape(self) -> None:
        """A dispatched version reaches tag names, asset file names and release
        titles. Grepping for the error message proves nothing — this finds the
        guard in each job and runs its regex, so a weakened pattern fails here
        rather than in a release."""
        source = (WORKFLOWS / "release.yml").read_text()
        self.assertIn("VERSION_INPUT", source)

        # Split into jobs so a guard in one cannot vouch for the other.
        jobs = dict(re.findall(r"^  (\w[\w-]*):\n(.*?)(?=^  \w[\w-]*:\n|\Z)",
                               source, re.M | re.S))
        for job in ("build", "publish"):
            self.assertIn(job, jobs, f"release.yml has no {job} job")
            guards = re.findall(r'\[\[ ! "\$version" =~ (\S+) \]\]', jobs[job])
            self.assertEqual(
                len(guards), 1,
                f"the {job} job must validate the version exactly once; found {len(guards)}",
            )
            self._assert_regex_is_strict(guards[0], job)

    ACCEPT = ["v0.1.0", "v1.2.3", "v10.20.30",
              "v1.2.3-nightly.202609192059.abc1234", "v0.0.0-dev.f9838c0", "v0.1.0+build.5"]
    REJECT = ["0.1.0", "v1.2", "v1", "", "v1.2.3.4", "v1.2.3-",
              "v1.2.3; rm -rf /", "v1.2.3$(id)", "v1.2.3 && echo pwned",
              "v1.2.3`id`", "../../etc/passwd", "v1.2.3\nv9.9.9"]

    def _assert_regex_is_strict(self, pattern: str, job: str) -> None:
        """Run the workflow's own regex in bash, the way the workflow does."""
        script = (
            'shopt -s nocasematch 2>/dev/null; '
            f'if [[ "$1" =~ {pattern} ]]; then echo ACCEPT; else echo REJECT; fi'
        )
        def verdict(value: str) -> str:
            return subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", script, "bash", value],
                                  capture_output=True, text=True,
                                  timeout=30).stdout.strip()

        for good in self.ACCEPT:
            self.assertEqual(verdict(good), "ACCEPT",
                             f"{job}: version {good!r} should be accepted by {pattern}")
        for bad in self.REJECT:
            self.assertEqual(verdict(bad), "REJECT",
                             f"{job}: version {bad!r} MUST be rejected by {pattern}")


class InstallerFailsClosed(unittest.TestCase):
    """The README and SECURITY.md both promise the downloaded archive is verified
    against the release checksums. Every path that would install without
    verifying must therefore be fatal."""

    def test_the_script_has_no_install_without_verification_path(self) -> None:
        source = INSTALLER.read_text()
        self.assertNotIn(
            "installing without verification",
            source,
            "the installer must not proceed when checksums.txt cannot be fetched",
        )
        self.assertNotIn(
            "skipping checksum verification",
            source,
            "the installer must not proceed when it has no tool to hash with",
        )

    def _run_with_fake_curl(self, checksums_status: int, want_dir: bool = False):
        """Run the installer with a curl stub on PATH that serves a tarball but
        answers the checksums.txt request with the given status."""
        tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, tmp, ignore_errors=True)

        payload = tmp / "payload"
        payload.mkdir()
        (payload / "entire-brain").write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho fake\n")
        subprocess.run(
            ["tar", "-czf", str(tmp / "asset.tar.gz"), "-C", str(payload), "entire-brain"],
            check=True,
        )

        fake_curl = tmp / "bin" / "curl"
        fake_curl.parent.mkdir()
        fake_curl.write_text(
            textwrap.dedent(
                f"""\
                #!/usr/bin/env bash
                # Serve the release archive, fail the checksums request.
                out=""
                url=""
                while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
                  case "$1" in
                    -o) out="$2"; shift 2 ;;
                    -*) shift ;;
                    *) url="$1"; shift ;;
                  esac
                done
                case "$url" in
                  *checksums.txt)
                    {"echo 'deadbeef  some-other-file.tar.gz' > \"$out\"; exit 0"
                     if checksums_status == 2 else
                     f"exit {1 if checksums_status else 0}"} ;;
                  *releases/latest) echo '{{"tag_name": "v9.9.9"}}'; exit 0 ;;
                  *.tar.gz) cp "{tmp / 'asset.tar.gz'}" "$out"; exit 0 ;;
                esac
                exit 0
                """
            )
        )
        fake_curl.chmod(fake_curl.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)

        # Stub `entire` too. The installer's success path runs
        # `entire plugin install --force`, which would repoint the developer's
        # real Brain plugin at this temp dir and then delete it on cleanup.
        # No test takes that path today; one added later must not break the host.
        fake_entire = fake_curl.parent / "entire"
        fake_entire.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 0\n")
        fake_entire.chmod(fake_entire.stat().st_mode | stat.S_IEXEC)

        env = dict(os.environ)
        env["PATH"] = f"{fake_curl.parent}:{env['PATH']}"
        env["ENTIRE_BRAIN_INSTALL_DIR"] = str(tmp / "install")

        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(INSTALLER), "--version", "v9.9.9"],
            capture_output=True,

1. Move the work into a `## [X.Y.Z]` section in `CHANGELOG.md`, dated.
2. Tag and push:

   ```sh

   ```

`windows` for both `amd64` and `arm64`, packages each as a `.tar.gz` (`.zip` on
Windows), writes `checksums.txt`, and creates the release with generated notes.
Re-running it against an existing tag updates that release rather than failing.

You can also run it from the Actions tab with a version, which is the way to
re-cut a release whose upload failed.

### Why one runner builds everything

Brain's default build is pure Go — both the SQLite driver and the vector path
have cgo-free implementations (`internal/cli/sqlite_driver_purego.go`,
`internal/cli/embed_vec_purego.go`), and SQLite itself comes from

release workflow asserts this rather than assuming it:

```yaml
- name: Verify the default build needs no cgo

```

release stops, instead of silently producing binaries that only run on the
build host.

93	# blackhole <dir> -> prints a port that accepts connections and never responds.
94	# A dead origin fails fast on connect; this is the nastier case — reachable, so
95	# curl waits. install.sh must still fail over.
96	blackhole() {
97	    local dir="$1" port
98	    mkdir -p "$dir"
99	    port="$(free_port)"
100	    python3 -c '
101	import socket, sys, time
102	srv = socket.socket()
103	srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
104	srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])))
105	srv.listen(16)
106	held = []
107	while True:
108	    conn, _ = srv.accept()
109	    held.append(conn)  # accepted, deliberately never answered
110	    time.sleep(0.01)
111	' "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
112	    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
113	    echo "$port"
114	}

116	free_port() {
117	    python3 -c 'import socket;s=socket.socket();s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0));print(s.getsockname()[1]);s.close()'
118	}

120	serve() { # <dir> -> prints the port it is listening on
121	    local dir="$1" port
122	    port="$(free_port)"
123	    ( cd "$dir" && exec python3 -m http.server "$port" --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &
124	    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
125	    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
126	        curl -fsS -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/" 2>/dev/null && break
127	        sleep 0.1
128	    done
129	    echo "$port"
130	}

132	# repoint <out> <our-origin> <github-origin> <github-api>
133	# A copy of install.sh with its origin constants aimed at local servers, so the
134	# two-tier chain runs without touching the network.
135	repoint() {
136	    sed -e "s|^DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN=.*|DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN=\"$2\"|" \
137	        -e "s|^GITHUB_RELEASE_ORIGIN=.*|GITHUB_RELEASE_ORIGIN=\"$3\"|" \
138	        -e "s|^GITHUB_API=.*|GITHUB_API=\"$4\"|" \
139	        "$INSTALL_SH" > "$1"

142	# run_install <home> <script> [args...]
143	#
144	# Runs install.sh with an empty environment and an isolated HOME, so it can
145	# never write to the developer's real ~/.local/bin. Set BASE_URL to point it at
146	# a local origin.
147	#
148	# env -i wipes the environment, so BASE_URL has to be re-injected explicitly —
149	# exporting it around the call is not enough. Getting that wrong made two cases
150	# silently download the real CLI from the real GitHub, so the guard below
151	# refuses to run a script that is still aimed at a public origin.
152	run_install() {
153	    local home="$1" script="$2"
154	    shift 2
155	    mkdir -p "$home"
156	
157	    local -a env_args=(HOME="$home" PATH="$SAFE_PATH" SHELL=/bin/bash)
158	    if [ -n "${BASE_URL:-}" ]; then
159	        env_args+=("ENTIRE_INSTALL_BASE_URL=$BASE_URL")
160	    elif ! grep -q '^DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN="http://127.0.0.1:' "$script"; then
161	        printf 'Error: %s would reach a public origin. Set BASE_URL or use repoint().\n' \
162	            "$(basename "$script")" >&2
163	        return 1
164	    fi
165	
166	    env -i "${env_args[@]}" bash "$script" "$@" 2>&1
167	}

355	section "publish-channel-manifest.sh"
356	
357	STUB_BIN="$WORK/stub-bin"
358	mkdir -p "$STUB_BIN"
359	cat > "$STUB_BIN/aws" <<'AWS'
360	#!/bin/bash
361	# Stub for the AWS CLI surface these scripts use, mapping s3://bucket/key and
362	# --bucket/--key to $AWS_STUB_ROOT/bucket/key.
363	#
364	#   s3 cp                 (publish-installers.sh)
365	#   s3api get-object      (publish-channel-manifest.sh, needs the ETag)
366	#   s3api put-object      (publish-channel-manifest.sh, conditional write)
367	#
368	# ETags are the content md5, as S3 does for a single-part upload, so --if-match
369	# behaves the way the real conditional write does.
370	set -uo pipefail
371	echo "$*" >> "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
372	
373	s3path() { printf '%s/%s' "$AWS_STUB_ROOT" "${1#s3://}"; }
374	etag_of() { md5 -q "$1" 2>/dev/null || md5sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }
375	not_found() {
376	    echo "fatal error: An error occurred (404) when calling the HeadObject operation: Not Found" >&2
377	    exit 1
378	}
379	
380	if [ "${1:-}" = "s3" ] && [ "${2:-}" = "cp" ]; then
381	    src="$3"; dst="$4"
382	    if [ -n "${AWS_STUB_READ_ERROR:-}" ] && [ "${src#s3://}" != "$src" ]; then
383	        echo "fatal error: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the HeadObject operation: Forbidden" >&2
384	        exit 1
385	    fi
386	    if [ "${src#s3://}" != "$src" ]; then
387	        f="$(s3path "$src")"; [ -f "$f" ] || not_found; cat "$f"; exit 0
388	    fi
389	    f="$(s3path "$dst")"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; cp "$src" "$f"; exit 0
390	fi
391	
392	if [ "${1:-}" = "s3api" ]; then
393	    op="$2"; shift 2
394	    bucket=""; key=""; body=""; outfile=""; if_match=""; if_none_match=""
395	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
396	        case "$1" in
397	            --bucket)         bucket="$2"; shift 2 ;;
398	            --key)            key="$2"; shift 2 ;;
399	            --body)           body="$2"; shift 2 ;;
400	            --if-match)       if_match="$2"; shift 2 ;;
401	            --if-none-match)  if_none_match="$2"; shift 2 ;;
402	            --region|--content-type|--cache-control) shift 2 ;;
403	            --*)              shift ;;
404	            *)                outfile="$1"; shift ;;
405	        esac
406	    done
407	    f="$AWS_STUB_ROOT/$bucket/$key"
408	
409	    case "$op" in
410	        get-object)
411	            [ -z "${AWS_STUB_READ_ERROR:-}" ] || {
412	                echo "fatal error: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the GetObject operation: Forbidden" >&2
413	                exit 1
414	            }
415	            [ -f "$f" ] || not_found
416	            [ -n "$outfile" ] && cp "$f" "$outfile"
417	            # AWS_STUB_STALE_ETAG reports an ETag that will not match at write
418	            # time, which is what a concurrent publisher looks like.
419	            if [ -n "${AWS_STUB_STALE_ETAG:-}" ]; then
420	                printf '{"ETag": "\"%s\"", "ContentType": "application/json"}\n' "stale00000000000000000000000000"
421	                exit 0
422	            fi
423	            printf '{"ETag": "\"%s\"", "ContentType": "application/json"}\n' "$(etag_of "$f")"
424	            exit 0 ;;
425	        put-object)
426	            if [ -n "$if_none_match" ] && [ -f "$f" ]; then
427	                echo "An error occurred (PreconditionFailed) when calling the PutObject operation: At least one of the pre-conditions you specified did not hold" >&2
428	                exit 1
429	            fi
430	            if [ -n "$if_match" ]; then
431	                [ -f "$f" ] || not_found
432	                if [ "$if_match" != "$(etag_of "$f")" ]; then
433	                    echo "An error occurred (PreconditionFailed) when calling the PutObject operation: At least one of the pre-conditions you specified did not hold" >&2
434	                    exit 1
435	                fi
436	            fi
437	            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; cp "$body" "$f"; exit 0 ;;
438	        *) exit 64 ;;
439	    esac
440	fi
441	
442	exit 64
443	AWS

505	expect "rejects a tag that is not semver" eq "$rc" 1
506	publish --bucket b >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
507	# A prerelease no channel claims is "nothing to publish", not a failed release:
508	# GoReleaser has already published by this point, so dying would fail the job
509	# after the fact, fire Slack and skip mirror-nightly.
510	fresh rctag
511	out="$(publish --tag v1.2.3-rc.1 --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
512	expect "an unclaimed prerelease is not a failure" contains "$out" "rc=0"
513	expect "it says no channel claims the tag" contains "$out" "No channel claims"
514	refute "no stable pointer is written" test -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/channels/stable.json"
515	refute "no nightly pointer is written" test -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/channels/nightly.json"
516	
517	# A tag that is not a version at all stays a hard error — that is a broken
518	# release, not an unclaimed one.
519	fresh junktag
520	out="$(publish --tag vnot-a-version --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
521	expect "a non-semver tag still fails" contains "$out" "rc=1"

523	# The publisher's nightly test must be the readers' test, not a looser one. A
524	# prerelease merely containing "nightly" would be routed to the channel, where
525	# the CLI accepts it and install.sh does not.
526	for t in v0.5.4-nightly v0.5.4-prenightly v0.5.4-rc.nightly.1; do
527	    fresh "nearmiss-$t"
528	    out="$(publish --tag "$t" --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
529	    refute "$t never reaches the nightly pointer" test -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/channels/nightly.json"
530	    expect "$t is reported as unclaimed" contains "$out" "No channel claims"
531	done
532	
533	fresh realnightly
534	out="$(publish --tag v0.5.4-nightly.202604061200.abc1234 --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
535	expect "a real nightly tag still publishes" contains "$out" "rc=0"
536	expect "it lands on the nightly channel" eq "$(pointer nightly)" "0.5.4-nightly.202604061200.abc1234"
537	
538	expect "requires --tag" eq "$rc" 1
539	
540	# The monotonic guard must fail closed: a pointer it could not read cannot be
541	# proven to be behind the version being published.
542	fresh readerr
543	seed stable 9.9.9
544	out="$(AWS_STUB_READ_ERROR=1 publish --tag v1.0.0 --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
545	expect "a non-404 read error refuses to publish" contains "$out" "rc=2"
546	expect "the refusal says the move cannot be proven forward" contains "$out" "cannot be proven to move it forward"
547	expect "the pointer is untouched after a read error" eq "$(pointer stable)" "9.9.9"
548	refute "a read error does not fall through to a backwards publish" contains "$out" "Refusing to move"
549	
550	# A manifest that exists but names no version is not an empty channel.
551	fresh unparseable
552	mkdir -p "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/channels"
553	printf '{"channel":"stable"}\n' > "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/channels/stable.json"
554	out="$(publish --tag v1.0.0 --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
555	expect "an unparseable pointer refuses to publish" contains "$out" "rc=2"
556	expect "the refusal names the object to inspect" contains "$out" "names no version"
557	
558	# The guard reads, compares and writes as three operations. A concurrent
559	# publisher landing in between would otherwise pass both guards and leave the
560	# pointer wherever the slower write finished.
561	fresh conflict
562	seed stable 1.0.0
563	out="$(AWS_STUB_STALE_ETAG=1 publish --tag v2.0.0 --bucket b; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
564	expect "a pointer that changed mid-publish is refused" contains "$out" "rc=2"
565	expect "the refusal says the comparison no longer holds" contains "$out" "no longer holds"
566	expect "the pointer is untouched after a conflict" eq "$(pointer stable)" "1.0.0"
567	
568	fresh conditional
569	publish --tag v1.0.0 --bucket b >/dev/null
570	expect "a first publish is conditional on the key being absent" \
571	    grep -qF -- "--if-none-match" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
572	publish --tag v1.1.0 --bucket b >/dev/null
573	expect "an update is conditional on the ETag it read" \
574	    grep -qF -- "--if-match" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
575	expect "the conditional update still moved the pointer" eq "$(pointer stable)" "1.1.0"
576	
577	printf '\n\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "publish-installers.sh"
578	
579	installers() { PATH="$STUB_BIN:$SAFE_PATH" bash "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/publish-installers.sh" "$@" 2>&1; }
580	
581	fresh installers
582	mkdir -p "$WORK/dist0/scoop"
583	cat > "$WORK/dist0/scoop/entire.json" <<'JSON'
584	{"version":"1.2.3","url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v1.2.3/entire_windows_amd64.zip","hash":"bbbb"}
585	JSON
586	out="$(installers --bucket b --dist "$WORK/dist0"; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
587	expect "publishes both installers" contains "$out" "rc=0"
588	expect "install.sh lands under installers/" \
589	    [ -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/installers/install.sh" ]
590	expect "install.ps1 lands under installers/" \
591	    [ -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/installers/install.ps1" ]
592	expect "the uploaded install.sh is the one in the repo" \
593	    cmp -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/install.sh" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/installers/install.sh"
594	
595	# Overwritten in place on every release, so a long TTL would pin a stale
596	# installer in every edge cache for the life of that TTL.
597	expect "installers get a short TTL, not the artifacts' immutable one" \
598	    grep -qF "max-age=300" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
599	refute "installers are not marked immutable" \
600	    grep -qF "immutable" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
601	
602	# Served through the Worker as-is: without an explicit type the script is
603	# offered as an octet-stream download instead of text anyone can read before
604	# piping it to a shell.
605	expect "install.sh is published as a shell script" \
606	    grep -qF "text/x-shellscript" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
607	expect "install.ps1 is published as readable text" \
608	    grep -qF "text/plain; charset=utf-8" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
609	
610	# Scoop installs from a manifest URL with no bucket and therefore no git, and
611	# records that URL as the app's source so `scoop update` re-fetches it. Verified
612	# against Scoop v0.6.0 on Windows. The mirrored manifest has to name this origin
613	# for its artifacts, because Scoop has no fallback of its own.
614	fresh scoopmanifest
615	mkdir -p "$WORK/dist/scoop"
616	cat > "$WORK/dist/scoop/entire.json" <<'JSON'
617	{
618	  "version": "1.2.3",
619	  "architecture": {
620	    "64bit": {
621	      "url": "https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v1.2.3/entire_windows_amd64.zip",
622	      "hash": "aaaa"
623	    }
624	  }
625	}
626	JSON
627	out="$(installers --bucket b --dist "$WORK/dist" --origin-url https://example.test; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
628	expect "publishes the scoop manifest" contains "$out" "rc=0"
629	expect "it lands at scoop/entire.json" test -f "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/scoop/entire.json"
630	expect "artifact urls are repointed at the origin" \
631	    grep -qF "https://example.test/v1.2.3/entire_windows_amd64.zip" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/scoop/entire.json"
632	refute "no GitHub download url survives" \
633	    grep -qF "github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/scoop/entire.json"
634	expect "the hash is left untouched" \
635	    grep -qF '"hash": "aaaa"' "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/b/scoop/entire.json"
636	expect "it is served as json" grep -qF "application/json" "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"
637	
638	# A silently un-rewritten manifest would publish fine and only fail during the
639	# outage it exists for, so the rewrite asserts it changed something.
640	fresh scoopunchanged
641	mkdir -p "$WORK/dist2/scoop"
642	printf '{"version":"1.2.3","url":"https://cdn.example.org/x.zip"}\n' > "$WORK/dist2/scoop/entire.json"
643	out="$(installers --bucket b --dist "$WORK/dist2" --origin-url https://example.test; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
644	expect "a manifest nothing was repointed in is refused" contains "$out" "rc=1"
645	expect "the refusal says nothing was repointed" contains "$out" "nothing was repointed"
646	
647	fresh scoopmissing
648	out="$(installers --bucket b --dist "$WORK/nope"; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
649	expect "a missing scoop manifest is an error, not a silent skip" contains "$out" "rc=1"
650	expect "the error names the path" contains "$out" "Scoop manifest not found"
651	
652	out="$(installers; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
653	expect "requires --bucket" contains "$out" "rc=1"
654	expect "the usage error names the missing flag" contains "$out" "--bucket is required"

#!/bin/bash
#
# Exercises the two-origin release path against local fake origins. No network,
# no writes outside a temp dir.
#
# Why this exists: install.sh reads our own release origin first and falls back
# to GitHub. The fallback only runs when something is broken, which is exactly
# when nobody wants to discover it never worked — so it is tested here instead
# of in production. Covers:
#
#   * install.sh resolving a version from channels/<channel>.json
#   * install.sh downloading and verifying from our origin
#   * install.sh falling back to the GitHub origin for both steps
#   * a checksum mismatch aborting instead of silently trying the next origin
#   * --version pinning, and the error text when every origin is unreachable
#   * publish-channel-manifest.sh routing, monotonicity and idempotence
#
# Requires: python3, curl, tar, sha256sum or shasum.
# Usage: scripts/test-release-origins.sh

set -uo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
INSTALL_SH="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/install.sh"
PUBLISH_SH="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/publish-channel-manifest.sh"
WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
# A PATH without the developer's real `entire`, so install.sh takes its
# first-time-install branch instead of the PATH-conflict branch.
SAFE_PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"

pass=0
fail=0
ok()   { printf '  \033[0;32mPASS\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
nope() { printf '  \033[0;31mFAIL\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }
section() { printf '\n\033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
indent() { while IFS= read -r line; do printf '      %s\n' "$line"; done; }

# expect <description> <command...> — passes when the command succeeds.
expect() {
    local desc="$1"
    shift
    if "$@"; then ok "$desc"; else nope "$desc"; fi
}

# refute <description> <command...> — passes when the command fails.
refute() {
    local desc="$1"
    shift
    if "$@"; then nope "$desc"; else ok "$desc"; fi
}

contains() { grep -qF -- "$2" <<< "$1"; }
eq()       { [ "$1" = "$2" ]; }

cleanup() {
    for pidfile in "$WORK"/*/.pid; do
        [ -f "$pidfile" ] && kill "$(cat "$pidfile")" 2>/dev/null
    done
    rm -rf "$WORK"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

sha256_of() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        sha256sum "$1"
    else
        shasum -a 256 "$1"
    fi
}

archive_name() {
    local os arch
    os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    arch="$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/; s/aarch64/arm64/')"
    printf 'entire_%s_%s.tar.gz' "$os" "$arch"
}

# build_origin <dir> <version> — a release tree shaped like both real origins:
# <root>/v<version>/{archive,checksums.txt} plus <root>/channels/*.json
build_origin() {
    local dir="$1" version="$2" arch
    arch="$(archive_name)"
    mkdir -p "$dir/v$version" "$dir/channels" "$dir/.stage"
    printf '#!/bin/sh\necho "entire %s"\n' "$version" > "$dir/.stage/entire"
    printf '#!/bin/sh\necho helper\n' > "$dir/.stage/git-remote-entire"
    chmod +x "$dir/.stage/entire" "$dir/.stage/git-remote-entire"
    tar -czf "$dir/v$version/$arch" -C "$dir/.stage" entire git-remote-entire
    ( cd "$dir/v$version" && sha256_of "$arch" > checksums.txt )
    printf '{"channel":"stable","tag":"v%s","version":"%s"}\n' "$version" "$version" \
        > "$dir/channels/stable.json"
}

# blackhole <dir> -> prints a port that accepts connections and never responds.
# A dead origin fails fast on connect; this is the nastier case — reachable, so
# curl waits. install.sh must still fail over.
blackhole() {
    local dir="$1" port
    mkdir -p "$dir"
    port="$(free_port)"
    python3 -c '
import socket, sys, time
srv = socket.socket()
srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", int(sys.argv[1])))
srv.listen(16)
held = []
while True:
    conn, _ = srv.accept()
    held.append(conn)  # accepted, deliberately never answered
    time.sleep(0.01)
' "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
    echo "$port"
}

free_port() {
    python3 -c 'import socket;s=socket.socket();s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0));print(s.getsockname()[1]);s.close()'
}

serve() { # <dir> -> prints the port it is listening on
    local dir="$1" port
    port="$(free_port)"
    ( cd "$dir" && exec python3 -m http.server "$port" --bind 127.0.0.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 ) &
    echo $! > "$dir/.pid"
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
        curl -fsS -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/" 2>/dev/null && break
        sleep 0.1
    done
    echo "$port"
}

# repoint <out> <our-origin> <github-origin> <github-api>
# A copy of install.sh with its origin constants aimed at local servers, so the
# two-tier chain runs without touching the network.
repoint() {
    sed -e "s|^DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN=.*|DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN=\"$2\"|" \
        -e "s|^GITHUB_RELEASE_ORIGIN=.*|GITHUB_RELEASE_ORIGIN=\"$3\"|" \
        -e "s|^GITHUB_API=.*|GITHUB_API=\"$4\"|" \
        "$INSTALL_SH" > "$1"
}

# run_install <home> <script> [args...]
#
# Runs install.sh with an empty environment and an isolated HOME, so it can
# never write to the developer's real ~/.local/bin. Set BASE_URL to point it at
# a local origin.
#
# env -i wipes the environment, so BASE_URL has to be re-injected explicitly —
# exporting it around the call is not enough. Getting that wrong made two cases
# silently download the real CLI from the real GitHub, so the guard below
# refuses to run a script that is still aimed at a public origin.
run_install() {
    local home="$1" script="$2"
    shift 2
    mkdir -p "$home"

    local -a env_args=(HOME="$home" PATH="$SAFE_PATH" SHELL=/bin/bash)
    if [ -n "${BASE_URL:-}" ]; then
        env_args+=("ENTIRE_INSTALL_BASE_URL=$BASE_URL")
    elif ! grep -q '^DEFAULT_RELEASE_ORIGIN="http://127.0.0.1:' "$script"; then
        printf 'Error: %s would reach a public origin. Set BASE_URL or use repoint().\n' \
            "$(basename "$script")" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    env -i "${env_args[@]}" bash "$script" "$@" 2>&1
}

for tool in python3 curl tar; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'Error: %s is required\n' "$tool" >&2; exit 1; }
done

# ============================================================ install.sh
section "install.sh — our origin first"

build_origin "$WORK/ours" 9.9.9
OURS_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/ours")"
OURS="http://127.0.0.1:$OURS_PORT"
ARCH="$(archive_name)"

out="$(BASE_URL="$OURS" run_install "$WORK/home-ours" "$INSTALL_SH")"
expect "resolves the version from channels/stable.json" contains "$out" "Installing version: 9.9.9"
expect "verifies the archive against our origin's checksums.txt" \
    contains "$out" "Checksum verified ($OURS)"
expect "installs entire" test -x "$WORK/home-ours/.local/bin/entire"
expect "installs git-remote-entire" test -x "$WORK/home-ours/.local/bin/git-remote-entire"
refute "does not touch GitHub when our origin answers" contains "$out" "github"

section "install.sh — falls back to GitHub"

build_origin "$WORK/gh" 8.8.8
mkdir -p "$WORK/gh/api/releases"
printf '{"tag_name":"v8.8.8","prerelease":false}\n' > "$WORK/gh/api/releases/latest"
GH_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/gh")"
GH="http://127.0.0.1:$GH_PORT"
DEAD="http://127.0.0.1:$(free_port)"

repoint "$WORK/install-fallback.sh" "$DEAD" "$GH" "$GH/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-fallback" "$WORK/install-fallback.sh")"
expect "falls back for version discovery" contains "$out" "Installing version: 8.8.8"
expect "falls back for the download" contains "$out" "Checksum verified (github.com/"
expect "the fallback install completes" test -x "$WORK/home-fallback/.local/bin/entire"

section "install.sh — a checksum mismatch aborts"

build_origin "$WORK/bad" 7.7.7
printf '%s  %s\n' "$(printf '0%.0s' $(seq 1 64))" "$ARCH" > "$WORK/bad/v7.7.7/checksums.txt"
BAD_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/bad")"
repoint "$WORK/install-badsum.sh" "http://127.0.0.1:$BAD_PORT" "$GH" "$GH/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-badsum" "$WORK/install-badsum.sh")"
rc=$?
refute "exits non-zero" eq "$rc" 0
expect "says the checksum failed" contains "$out" "Checksum verification failed"
refute "installs nothing" test -e "$WORK/home-badsum/.local/bin/entire"
refute "does not fall back after a mismatch" contains "$out" "Checksum verified"

section "install.sh — pinning and unreachable origins"

out="$(BASE_URL="$OURS" run_install "$WORK/home-pin" "$INSTALL_SH" --version v9.9.9)"
refute "--version skips version discovery" contains "$out" "Fetching latest"
expect "--version installs" test -x "$WORK/home-pin/.local/bin/entire"

repoint "$WORK/install-alldown.sh" "$DEAD" "$DEAD" "$DEAD/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-alldown" "$WORK/install-alldown.sh")"
rc=$?
refute "every origin down exits non-zero" eq "$rc" 0
expect "the error names the pinning escape hatch" contains "$out" "--version X.Y.Z"

section "install.sh — a hanging origin still fails over"

# Shortens the real policy rather than substituting a different one. The
# download path has no --max-time in production — injecting one here would make
# this pass on a bound that does not exist, which is exactly the failure it is
# supposed to catch. So the metadata budget shrinks (it already has --max-time)
# and the download keeps --speed-limit/--speed-time with a 2s window.
BH_PORT="$(blackhole "$WORK/blackhole")"
repoint "$WORK/install-hang.sh" "http://127.0.0.1:$BH_PORT" "$GH" "$GH/api"
sed -i.bak \
    -e 's|^CURL_METADATA_OPTS=.*|CURL_METADATA_OPTS=(--connect-timeout 1 --max-time 2)|' \
    -e 's|^CURL_DOWNLOAD_OPTS=.*|CURL_DOWNLOAD_OPTS=(--connect-timeout 1 --speed-limit 1 --speed-time 2)|' \
    "$WORK/install-hang.sh"
started="$(date +%s)"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-hang" "$WORK/install-hang.sh")"
elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - started ))
expect "falls over to GitHub instead of hanging" contains "$out" "Installing version: 8.8.8"
expect "the install completes despite the hung origin" test -x "$WORK/home-hang/.local/bin/entire"
expect "gives up on the hung origin within the budget" test "$elapsed" -lt 20

# ============================================================ channel pointer
section "install.sh — the GitHub fallback is held to the same rules"

# The fallback used a bare "nightly" substring and validated nothing, so the two
# origins in this script disagreed about what counts as installable.
build_origin "$WORK/ghloose" 5.5.5
mkdir -p "$WORK/ghloose/api"
# Pretty-printed, one "tag_name" per line, as the real API returns it. A
# single-line fixture never exercises the per-line filter this guards.
cat > "$WORK/ghloose/api/releases" <<'JSON'
[
  {
    "tag_name": "v4.4.4-prenightly",
    "prerelease": true
  },
  {
    "tag_name": "v3.3.3-nightly.202604061200.abc1234",
    "prerelease": true
  }
]
JSON
GHLOOSE_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/ghloose")"
GHL="http://127.0.0.1:$GHLOOSE_PORT"
DEADL="http://127.0.0.1:$(free_port)"
build_origin "$WORK/ghloose" 3.3.3-nightly.202604061200.abc1234
repoint "$WORK/install-ghloose.sh" "$DEADL" "$GHL" "$GHL/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-ghloose" "$WORK/install-ghloose.sh" --channel nightly)"
expect "a near-miss nightly tag is skipped on the fallback too" \
    contains "$out" "Installing version: 3.3.3-nightly.202604061200.abc1234"
refute "the near-miss tag is never selected" contains "$out" "prenightly"

section "install.sh — --version is validated on its own"

# It is interpolated into ${base}/v${version}/..., and curl normalises ".."
# segments, so an unchecked value addresses something outside the version
# prefix and fails later as a generic download error.
repoint "$WORK/install-badver.sh" "$DEAD" "$GH" "$GH/api"
for bad in "../../y" "not-a-version" "1.2"; do
    out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-badver" "$WORK/install-badver.sh" --version "$bad"; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
    refute "--version $bad does not reach a download" contains "$out" "Installing version"
    expect "--version $bad is rejected as not a version" contains "$out" "is not a version"
done

section "install.sh — --version and --channel cannot contradict"

repoint "$WORK/install-conflict.sh" "$DEAD" "$GH" "$GH/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-conflict" "$WORK/install-conflict.sh" --channel nightly --version 0.11.0; printf 'rc=%s' "$?")"
refute "a stable version under --channel nightly is not installed" contains "$out" "Installing version: 0.11.0"
expect "it says the version is not of that channel" contains "$out" "is not a nightly version"

section "install.sh — unusable manifest metadata falls back"

# A version that is not a version must not end discovery. Both origins would
# then be asked for a release that does not exist, failing the install even
# though GitHub has a valid one.
build_origin "$WORK/badmeta" 5.5.5
printf '{"channel":"stable","tag":"vnot-a-version","version":"not-a-version"}\n' \
    > "$WORK/badmeta/channels/stable.json"
BADMETA_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/badmeta")"
repoint "$WORK/install-badmeta.sh" "http://127.0.0.1:$BADMETA_PORT" "$GH" "$GH/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-badmeta" "$WORK/install-badmeta.sh")"
expect "a manifest naming a non-version falls back to GitHub" contains "$out" "Installing version: 8.8.8"
expect "the install completes from the fallback" test -x "$WORK/home-badmeta/.local/bin/entire"
refute "the bad version is never requested" contains "$out" "not-a-version"

# A nightly on the stable channel is the cross-stream case: accepting it would
# move every stable install onto a prerelease.
build_origin "$WORK/crossmeta" 6.6.6
printf '{"channel":"stable","version":"4.4.4-nightly.202604061200.abc1234"}\n' \
    > "$WORK/crossmeta/channels/stable.json"
CROSS_PORT="$(serve "$WORK/crossmeta")"
repoint "$WORK/install-crossmeta.sh" "http://127.0.0.1:$CROSS_PORT" "$GH" "$GH/api"
out="$(run_install "$WORK/home-crossmeta" "$WORK/install-crossmeta.sh")"
expect "a nightly on the stable channel falls back to GitHub" contains "$out" "Installing version: 8.8.8"
refute "the nightly version is never installed" contains "$out" "4.4.4-nightly"

# The CLI reads tag before version and checks the declared channel; install.sh
# has to agree or the two disagree about what is installable.
build_origin "$WORK/tagpref" 3.3.3
printf '{"channel":"stable","tag":"v3.3.3","version":"9.9.9"}\n' \
    > "$WORK/tagpref/channels/stable.json"

STUB_BIN="$WORK/stub-bin"
mkdir -p "$STUB_BIN"
cat > "$STUB_BIN/aws" <<'AWS'
#!/bin/bash
# Stub for the AWS CLI surface these scripts use, mapping s3://bucket/key and
# --bucket/--key to $AWS_STUB_ROOT/bucket/key.
#
#   s3 cp                 (publish-installers.sh)
#   s3api get-object      (publish-channel-manifest.sh, needs the ETag)
#   s3api put-object      (publish-channel-manifest.sh, conditional write)
#
# ETags are the content md5, as S3 does for a single-part upload, so --if-match
# behaves the way the real conditional write does.
set -uo pipefail
echo "$*" >> "$AWS_STUB_ROOT/calls.log"

s3path() { printf '%s/%s' "$AWS_STUB_ROOT" "${1#s3://}"; }
etag_of() { md5 -q "$1" 2>/dev/null || md5sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }
not_found() {
    echo "fatal error: An error occurred (404) when calling the HeadObject operation: Not Found" >&2
    exit 1
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "s3" ] && [ "${2:-}" = "cp" ]; then
    src="$3"; dst="$4"
    if [ -n "${AWS_STUB_READ_ERROR:-}" ] && [ "${src#s3://}" != "$src" ]; then
        echo "fatal error: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the HeadObject operation: Forbidden" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if [ "${src#s3://}" != "$src" ]; then
        f="$(s3path "$src")"; [ -f "$f" ] || not_found; cat "$f"; exit 0
    fi
    f="$(s3path "$dst")"; mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; cp "$src" "$f"; exit 0
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = "s3api" ]; then
    op="$2"; shift 2
    bucket=""; key=""; body=""; outfile=""; if_match=""; if_none_match=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --bucket)         bucket="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --key)            key="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --body)           body="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --if-match)       if_match="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --if-none-match)  if_none_match="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --region|--content-type|--cache-control) shift 2 ;;
            --*)              shift ;;
            *)                outfile="$1"; shift ;;
        esac
    done
    f="$AWS_STUB_ROOT/$bucket/$key"

    case "$op" in
        get-object)
            [ -z "${AWS_STUB_READ_ERROR:-}" ] || {
                echo "fatal error: An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the GetObject operation: Forbidden" >&2
                exit 1
            }
            [ -f "$f" ] || not_found
            [ -n "$outfile" ] && cp "$f" "$outfile"
            # AWS_STUB_STALE_ETAG reports an ETag that will not match at write
            # time, which is what a concurrent publisher looks like.
            if [ -n "${AWS_STUB_STALE_ETAG:-}" ]; then
                printf '{"ETag": "\"%s\"", "ContentType": "application/json"}\n' "stale00000000000000000000000000"
                exit 0
            fi
            printf '{"ETag": "\"%s\"", "ContentType": "application/json"}\n' "$(etag_of "$f")"
            exit 0 ;;
        put-object)
            if [ -n "$if_none_match" ] && [ -f "$f" ]; then
                echo "An error occurred (PreconditionFailed) when calling the PutObject operation: At least one of the pre-conditions you specified did not hold" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
            if [ -n "$if_match" ]; then
                [ -f "$f" ] || not_found
                if [ "$if_match" != "$(etag_of "$f")" ]; then
                    echo "An error occurred (PreconditionFailed) when calling the PutObject operation: At least one of the pre-conditions you specified did not hold" >&2
                    exit 1
                fi
            fi
            mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")"; cp "$body" "$f"; exit 0 ;;
        *) exit 64 ;;
    esac
fi

exit 64
AWS
chmod +x "$STUB_BIN/aws"

//
// Once built as an executable named `entire-brain`, the parent Entire CLI

package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli"
)

var version = "dev"

func main() {
	if err := cli.Execute(version); err != nil {
		if !errors.Is(err, cli.RenderedError()) {

		}
		os.Exit(1)
	}

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# Release configuration for entire-brain. Modelled on the Entire CLI's
# (entireio/cli/.goreleaser.yaml); see docs/releasing.md for how the pieces fit
# together and what has to be configured outside this repository.
#
# Open-source GoReleaser is enough: nothing here needs Pro, so the release does
# not depend on a license key.
version: 2

project_name: entire-brain

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod download

builds:
  - id: entire-brain
    main: ./cmd/entire-brain
    binary: entire-brain
    # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo variant
    # was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278), so every target
    # cross-compiles from one Linux runner. release.yml asserts this before
    # GoReleaser runs.
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    # Pin the binary mtime to the commit so rebuilding a tag produces identical
    # bytes. Files under brain/v<version>/ on the release origin are cached
    # immutable for a year; a retried release that re-uploaded different bytes
    # would leave an edge holding the old archive beside the new checksums.txt,
    # and the installer deliberately aborts on a checksum mismatch.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }}

notarize:
  macos:
    # Tests non-emptiness, not isEnvSet alone: release.yml always exports these
    # variables, and a secret that is not configured exports as an empty
    # string. Gating on presence would enable signing with no certificate and
    # fail every release instead of staying off.
    - enabled: '{{ and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}'
      ids:
        - entire-brain
      sign:
        certificate: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}"
        password: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}"
        key_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}"
        key: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    # The versioned name every Brain release has used. scripts/get-brain.sh
    # builds it, and the Entire CLI's plugin fetcher (plugin_fetch.go,
    # assetCandidates) tries <bin>_<version>_<os>_<arch> first.
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

# Mirror every release artifact to the release origin, install.entire.com, so
# installing keeps working while GitHub is down. The origin is a Cloudflare
# Worker that maps /<path> to the bucket key <path> verbatim, and the Entire CLI
# owns the bucket's top-level v*/, channels/ and installers/ prefixes, so
# everything Brain publishes lives under brain/.
#
# Layout is brain/v<version>/<file>, deliberately the same shape as GitHub's
# releases/download/v<version>/<file>, so get-brain.sh builds both origins' URLs
# from one template.
#
# Inert until ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET is set to a non-empty value. The variable is
# always exported by release.yml, and an unset Actions variable exports as an
# empty string, so isEnvSet alone would be true on every release and enable
# this pipe with no bucket and no credentials. scripts/test-release-origins.sh
# pins this.
blobs:
  - provider: s3
    disable: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'
    bucket: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET }}{{ else }}unset{{ end }}'
    region: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION }}{{ else }}us-east-2{{ end }}'
    directory: "brain/v{{ .Version }}"
    # A file under a version prefix never changes once published. The channel
    # pointers, which do change, are uploaded separately with a short TTL by
    # scripts/publish-channel-manifest.sh.
    cache_control:
      - "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

release:
  prerelease: auto

scoops:
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    license: MIT
    # The Entire CLI finds entire-brain on PATH, so `entire brain` works as
    # soon as Scoop's shim is in place.
    post_install:
      - "Write-Host 'Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup' -ForegroundColor Green"
    skip_upload: auto

homebrew_casks:
  # Casks are quarantined on download, so an unsigned binary would be killed by
  # Gatekeeper on first launch. Both casks are therefore published only when
  # the macOS signing secrets are configured; release.yml then also verifies
  # that the darwin binaries really are Developer ID signed.
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    binaries:
      - entire-brain
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire-brain@nightly
    caveats: "Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup"
    skip_upload: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}auto{{ else }}true{{ end }}'

  - name: entire-brain@nightly
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain (nightly build)"
    binaries:
      - entire-brain
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire-brain
    caveats: "Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup"
    skip_upload: '{{ if and .Prerelease (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'

    binary: entire-brain
    # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo variant
    # was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278), so every target
    # cross-compiles from one Linux runner. release.yml asserts this before
    # GoReleaser runs.
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    # Pin the binary mtime to the commit so rebuilding a tag produces identical
    # bytes. Files under brain/v<version>/ on the release origin are cached
    # immutable for a year; a retried release that re-uploaded different bytes
    # would leave an edge holding the old archive beside the new checksums.txt,
    # and the installer deliberately aborts on a checksum mismatch.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }}

notarize:
  macos:
    # Tests non-emptiness, not isEnvSet alone: release.yml always exports these
    # variables, and a secret that is not configured exports as an empty
    # string. Gating on presence would enable signing with no certificate and
    # fail every release instead of staying off.
    - enabled: '{{ and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}'
      ids:
        - entire-brain
      sign:
        certificate: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}"
        password: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}"
        key_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}"
        key: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    # The versioned name every Brain release has used. scripts/get-brain.sh
    # builds it, and the Entire CLI's plugin fetcher (plugin_fetch.go,
    # assetCandidates) tries <bin>_<version>_<os>_<arch> first.
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

# Mirror every release artifact to the release origin, install.entire.com, so
# installing keeps working while GitHub is down. The origin is a Cloudflare
# Worker that maps /<path> to the bucket key <path> verbatim, and the Entire CLI
# owns the bucket's top-level v*/, channels/ and installers/ prefixes, so
# everything Brain publishes lives under brain/.
#
# Layout is brain/v<version>/<file>, deliberately the same shape as GitHub's
# releases/download/v<version>/<file>, so get-brain.sh builds both origins' URLs
# from one template.
#
# Inert until ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET is set to a non-empty value. The variable is
# always exported by release.yml, and an unset Actions variable exports as an
# empty string, so isEnvSet alone would be true on every release and enable
# this pipe with no bucket and no credentials. scripts/test-release-origins.sh
# pins this.
blobs:
  - provider: s3
    disable: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'
    bucket: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET }}{{ else }}unset{{ end }}'
    region: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION }}{{ else }}us-east-2{{ end }}'
    directory: "brain/v{{ .Version }}"
    # A file under a version prefix never changes once published. The channel
    # pointers, which do change, are uploaded separately with a short TTL by
    # scripts/publish-channel-manifest.sh.
    cache_control:
      - "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

release:
  prerelease: auto

scoops:
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    license: MIT
    # The Entire CLI finds entire-brain on PATH, so `entire brain` works as
    # soon as Scoop's shim is in place.
    post_install:
      - "Write-Host 'Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup' -ForegroundColor Green"
    skip_upload: auto

homebrew_casks:
  # Casks are quarantined on download, so an unsigned binary would be killed by
  # Gatekeeper on first launch. Both casks are therefore published only when
  # the macOS signing secrets are configured; release.yml then also verifies
  # that the darwin binaries really are Developer ID signed.
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    binaries:
      - entire-brain
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire-brain@nightly
    caveats: "Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup"
    skip_upload: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}auto{{ else }}true{{ end }}'

  - name: entire-brain@nightly
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain (nightly build)"
    binaries:

      - cask: entire-brain

    skip_upload: '{{ if and .Prerelease (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema.json
#
# Release configuration for entire-brain. Modelled on the Entire CLI's
# (entireio/cli/.goreleaser.yaml); see docs/releasing.md for how the pieces fit
# together and what has to be configured outside this repository.
#
# Open-source GoReleaser is enough: nothing here needs Pro, so the release does
# not depend on a license key.
version: 2

project_name: entire-brain

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod download

builds:
  - id: entire-brain
    main: ./cmd/entire-brain
    binary: entire-brain
    # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo variant
    # was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278), so every target
    # cross-compiles from one Linux runner. release.yml asserts this before
    # GoReleaser runs.
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    flags:
      - -trimpath
    # Pin the binary mtime to the commit so rebuilding a tag produces identical
    # bytes. Files under brain/v<version>/ on the release origin are cached
    # immutable for a year; a retried release that re-uploaded different bytes
    # would leave an edge holding the old archive beside the new checksums.txt,
    # and the installer deliberately aborts on a checksum mismatch.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"
    ldflags:
      - -s -w -X main.version={{ .Version }}

notarize:
  macos:
    # Tests non-emptiness, not isEnvSet alone: release.yml always exports these
    # variables, and a secret that is not configured exports as an empty
    # string. Gating on presence would enable signing with no certificate and
    # fail every release instead of staying off.
    - enabled: '{{ and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}'
      ids:
        - entire-brain
      sign:
        certificate: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 }}"
        password: "{{ .Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD }}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID }}"
        key_id: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID }}"
        key: "{{ .Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY }}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    # The versioned name every Brain release has used. scripts/get-brain.sh
    # builds it, and the Entire CLI's plugin fetcher (plugin_fetch.go,
    # assetCandidates) tries <bin>_<version>_<os>_<arch> first.
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

# Mirror every release artifact to the release origin, install.entire.com, so
# installing keeps working while GitHub is down. The origin is a Cloudflare
# Worker that maps /<path> to the bucket key <path> verbatim, and the Entire CLI
# owns the bucket's top-level v*/, channels/ and installers/ prefixes, so
# everything Brain publishes lives under brain/.
#
# Layout is brain/v<version>/<file>, deliberately the same shape as GitHub's
# releases/download/v<version>/<file>, so get-brain.sh builds both origins' URLs
# from one template.
#
# Inert until ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET is set to a non-empty value. The variable is
# always exported by release.yml, and an unset Actions variable exports as an
# empty string, so isEnvSet alone would be true on every release and enable
# this pipe with no bucket and no credentials. scripts/test-release-origins.sh
# pins this.
blobs:
  - provider: s3
    disable: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'
    bucket: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_BUCKET }}{{ else }}unset{{ end }}'
    region: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION") (ne .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION "") }}{{ .Env.ENTIRE_RELEASE_REGION }}{{ else }}us-east-2{{ end }}'
    directory: "brain/v{{ .Version }}"
    # A file under a version prefix never changes once published. The channel
    # pointers, which do change, are uploaded separately with a short TTL by
    # scripts/publish-channel-manifest.sh.
    cache_control:
      - "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"

release:
  prerelease: auto

scoops:
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    license: MIT
    # The Entire CLI finds entire-brain on PATH, so `entire brain` works as
    # soon as Scoop's shim is in place.
    post_install:
      - "Write-Host 'Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup' -ForegroundColor Green"
    skip_upload: auto

homebrew_casks:
  # Casks are quarantined on download, so an unsigned binary would be killed by
  # Gatekeeper on first launch. Both casks are therefore published only when
  # the macOS signing secrets are configured; release.yml then also verifies
  # that the darwin binaries really are Developer ID signed.
  - name: entire-brain
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain: retained knowledge, history and task context for your repository"
    binaries:
      - entire-brain
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire-brain@nightly
    caveats: "Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup"
    skip_upload: '{{ if and (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}auto{{ else }}true{{ end }}'

  - name: entire-brain@nightly
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain"
    description: "Entire Brain (nightly build)"
    binaries:
      - entire-brain
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire-brain
    caveats: "Run it through the Entire CLI: entire brain setup"
    skip_upload: '{{ if and .Prerelease (isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12") (ne .Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12 "") }}false{{ else }}true{{ end }}'
